lesson_title: Cutting the Loaf: Ratio, Rate and Proportion
hook_text: Two bags of rice. One is cheaper. Your eyes cannot tell you which — but one division can.
clip_script: Two bags on the shelf. Two kilograms for R56,99. Ten kilograms for R249,99. Which one is actually cheaper? Your eyes cannot referee this, because the bags are different sizes. So do what gogo does — bring both down to ONE kilogram. R56,99 shared over 2 kilograms: about R28,50 a kilogram. R249,99 shared over ten: R25,00 a kilogram. The big bag wins, by roughly R3,50 every single kilogram. That's about thirty-five rand back in your pocket. And it's the same move everywhere. Car does 560 kilometres on 40 litres? Fourteen kilometres per litre. Water at R16,80 a kilolitre, you used 15? R252. Price of ONE, times how many. Now the grown-up part: cheaper per kilogram is only better if you HAVE the R249,99 today, and if the rice gets eaten before the weevils find it. Say the number — then say the condition. That's a complete answer, and complete answers get the tick.
visual_style: A supermarket aisle at eye level: two rice bags, price tags glowing, then both dissolving into a single one-kilogram scoop with a rand figure above it; quick cuts to a car fuel gauge and a water meter counting kilolitres.
mood: Warm, streetwise, quietly triumphant — the confidence of someone who never gets overcharged.
pacing: Slow curious open on the two bags, brisk middle through the divisions, calm settled close on the condition.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never guess at a shelf price again.
